literal: Even having forgotten, another's ruin let one not plan; if planned, virtue will plan the planner's ruin.
translation: Do not plot the ruin of another, even in a moment of forgetfulness. If you do, virtue itself will plot your ruin.
modern: மறந்துபோய்கூட மற்றொருவனுக்குக் கேடு செய்ய நினைக்கக் கூடாது; அப்படி நினைத்தால், நினைத்தவனுக்குக் கேடு செய்ய அறமே நினைக்கும்.
explanation: This couplet warns against plotting harm to others, emphasizing that such thoughts should not occur even by accident or forgetfulness. The word 'சூழற்க' (let one not plan) highlights that the mere intention or plotting of evil is forbidden. If one does plot another's ruin, 'அறம்' (virtue or the moral order) will turn against them and actively plan their downfall. Thus, the moral law acts as an inevitable force of justice against those who harbor malicious intentions.
